On H200, peak FP32 FFMA is 67 TFLOPS while TF32 Tensor Core peak is 989 TFLOPS — roughly 14.8x higher. The kernel achieves only 7.93% compute SOL and 6.25% occupancy. Enabling TF32 (allow_tf32=True) routes tl.dot through the Tensor Core MMA pipeline, dramatically increasing compute throughput. strategy_title: Reducing BLOCK_K Alone Cannot Fix Smem Bank Conflicts
strategy_description: Reducing BLOCK_K from 128 to 32 (and increasing BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N from 32 to 64) partially reduced per-instruction MIO stall cycles (7.34→4.26 cycles/instruction) and reduced shared memory per block (65→33 KB), but the total executed instruction count exploded 3.2x (3.1M→10.0M instructions), causing overall kernel duration to nearly double (49.6→91.5 µs). The bank conflict rate remained at ~12-way on 77-78% of shared load wavefronts, meaning the access pattern conflict was not resolved by the tile size change alone. The register pressure also increased significantly (94→128 registers/thread), further limiting occupancy. When the dominant bottleneck is shared memory bank conflicts, simply changing tile dimensions without fixing the underlying strided access pattern (e.g., adding padding to shared memory arrays or transposing the load layout) will not eliminate conflicts and may dramatically increase instruction count.
slow_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=128 (hardcoded)
# 12-way smem bank conflicts on 77.78% of shared loads
# Duration: 49.6 us, 3.1M instructions
for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K=128):
    a_tile = load_A(BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_K=128)  # smem
    b_tile = load_B(BLOCK_K=128, BLOCK_N=32)  # smem, strided access -> 12-way conflict
    acc += dot(a_tile, b_tile)
fast_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32 (changed)
# Still 12-way smem bank conflicts on 77.71% of shared loads
# Duration: 91.5 us, 10.0M instructions (3.2x more work!)
for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K=32):  # 26 iterations instead of 6.5
    a_tile = load_A(BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_K=32)  # smem
    b_tile = load_B(BLOCK_K=32, BLOCK_N=64)  # smem, still conflicted
    acc += dot(a_tile, b_tile)  # more iterations = more total instructions
applicable_when: Never: this specific approach (reducing BLOCK_K without fixing the access pattern) is always harmful when bank conflicts persist.
do_not_apply_when: When shared memory bank conflicts are caused by strided access patterns (e.g., column-major loads into row-major shared memory), reducing BLOCK_K alone does not change the conflict structure and causes a multiplicative increase in loop iterations and total instruction count. Do not apply tile size reduction as the sole fix for bank conflicts without also padding shared memory arrays or transposing the load layout to achieve conflict-free access.
framework_notes: In Triton, shared memory bank conflicts arise from the access stride pattern within tl.load into shared memory. Padding the shared memory tile dimension by 1 element (e.g., BLOCK_K+1 instead of BLOCK_K for the inner dimension) is the canonical fix. Tile size changes alone do not alter the bank conflict structure if the stride pattern remains the same.
